hints: Focus on what the sign really means, positive is heat taken in from surroundings and negative is heat given out to surroundings.
Remember the golden rule, breaking a chemical bond always needs energy put in, so it is endothermic.
Link this to familiar reactions, neutralisation and combustion both warm up the solution or surroundings, so decide which sign they must have.
walkthrough:
**Understand the signs**

Think like an energy accountant. If the chemicals gain energy, $\Delta H$ is positive (endothermic). If they lose energy as heat, $\Delta H$ is negative (exothermic).

**Bond breaking versus bond making**

To pull atoms apart you must put energy in, so bond breaking is always $\Delta H$ positive.

When atoms join together, energy is released, so bond making is always $\Delta H$ negative:
$$\text{bond breaking: } \Delta H > 0, \quad \text{bond making: } \Delta H < 0$$

**Apply to familiar processes**

Atomisation turns a solid into separate gaseous atoms, so it breaks bonds and is positive. Neutralisation, $\text{H}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}$, and combustion both form new bonds and release heat, so they are negative. Only the row with bond breaking as positive and neutralisation as negative fits both rules.

options.A: Atomisation is correctly positive because gaseous atoms are made from the element, which needs energy. But bond breaking is also positive, not negative, because energy must be supplied to separate atoms.
options.B: Bond breaking needs an input of energy so $\Delta H$ is positive. Neutralisation forms water from $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{OH}^-$ and releases heat to the surroundings, so $\Delta H$ is negative. Both columns are correct.
options.C: Combustion is correctly negative because burning releases heat. But bond making is also negative, not positive, because forming bonds releases energy.
options.D: Bond making is correctly negative, but combustion is also negative, not positive. Combustion is a classic exothermic reaction that always gives out heat.
